definition: Understood by or intended for a small group with specialized knowledge.
example: The footnote addressed an esoteric dispute among textual scholars.
nuance: Esoteric need not mean secret; the audience may simply need specialist knowledge.
prompt: A discussion assumes knowledge of a specialized branch of mathematics.
options: The lecture explored esoteric notation familiar only to specialists in the field.
The esoteric lecture explained everyday facts that everyone already understood.
The esoteric lecture was brief enough to fit into five minutes.
The esoteric lecture served tropical fruit flown in from distant islands.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: understood by or intended for a small group with specialized knowledge.
Widely understood everyday facts are not specialized or restricted in audience.
Length does not establish whether knowledge is esoteric.
This confuses the word with exotic; foreign or colorful things are not thereby specialized knowledge.

practice.prompt: A podcast about medieval bookbinding uses technical terms its hosts never explain.
options: The esoteric episode had background music so loud it drowned out the hosts.
Newcomers were lost in the esoteric jargon, but veteran binders nodded along.
The hosts kept every topic esoteric so that any casual listener could follow along instantly.
The esoteric hosts posted episodes at random, sometimes daily and sometimes months apart.
reasons: How loud the music is says nothing about who is able to understand the content.
Jargon that only experienced practitioners can follow is aimed at a narrow, expert audience.
Content that any casual listener grasps at once is the opposite of specialist material.
This confuses the word with erratic; an irregular schedule has nothing to do with expertise.
